original_question: If two spherical space forms have the same length spectrum of closed geodesics, must they be quotient commensurable, meaning that both arise as finite-index quotients inside a common finite group generated by their deck groups?
target_in_paper: Question 8.9 in Section 8.4, “The length spectra of spherical space forms.” ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual open problem: it has the correct objects (spherical space forms), the correct hypothesis (same length spectrum of closed geodesics), and the correct intended conclusion (quotient commensurability). It also points toward the paper’s adjacent group-theoretic reformulation via the deck groups. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s ambient objects are spherical space forms of the form M = S^d/Γ, with the round metric of constant sectional curvature 1, where Γ is a finite subgroup of O(d+1) acting freely on S^d; this realization is implicit in your draft and should be stated to make the question stand-alone. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))

In the surrounding context, the length spectrum is defined as the set of lengths of closed geodesics; the paper does not phrase it here as a multiplicity-weighted spectrum, so that should be made explicit. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))

“Quotient commensurable” is defined geometrically as admitting a common finite-degree quotient manifold; your draft gives only the group-theoretic intuition and omits this primary definition. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))

The nearby equivalent reformulation is precise only after writing the space forms as S^d/Γ1 and S^d/Γ2: they are quotient commensurable if and only if Γ1 and Γ2 both have finite index in G = ⟨Γ1, Γ2⟩. Your phrase “inside a common finite group” is not quite faithful, because the paper does not assume G is finite a priori; finiteness follows if the finite-index condition holds. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))

To match the paper’s nearby reformulation cleanly, a common dimension d should be fixed in the stand-alone version by writing both manifolds as quotients of the same sphere S^d. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))
refined_question: Let M = S^d/Γ1 and N = S^d/Γ2 be d-dimensional spherical space forms, where Γ1, Γ2 ≤ O(d+1) are finite subgroups acting freely on the round sphere S^d, and let M and N carry the induced Riemannian metrics of constant sectional curvature 1. If M and N have the same length spectrum, meaning the same set of lengths of closed geodesics, must M and N be quotient commensurable; that is, must they admit a common finite-degree quotient manifold? ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for M = S^d/Γ1 and N = S^d/Γ2, does equality of length spectra force Γ1 and Γ2 to both have finite index in the subgroup G = ⟨Γ1, Γ2⟩ ≤ O(d+1)? ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))
justification: The exact target is the paper’s open Question 8.9 in Section 8.4. The surrounding text in the same subsection supplies the needed definitions of length spectrum and quotient commensurability, including the explicit equivalence with the finite-index condition in G = ⟨Γ1, Γ2⟩ for spherical space forms written as S^d/Γi. Section 2 supplies the ambient model of a spherical space form as a free finite quotient of the round sphere. The rewrite therefore adds only those implicit hypotheses and definitions needed to make the question self-contained, without broadening it beyond the paper’s intended scope. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))
